items.notes: Quote: 'A concurrent DeleteEntry that lands between the EXISTS and the ZAddNX leaves a member with no value ... The window is small and it self-heals'. The interleaving is real (l.245-250) but, as the item itself says, the result is a fresh orphan that the next listing repairs, not a lost live entry; register rules the single-view concurrent race converges. 'if the EXISTS errors, the member is restored blindly' is the PR's deliberate bias toward a stale member. Below threshold.

Quote: 'The pre-existing logical-expiry branch in the same loop has the same race, and it is worse.' Register non_defects: the TTL-expiry branch (l.214-218) race is true but preexisting, unchanged by the diff, disclosed in the PR body.

Quote: 'The not-found branch still logs at glog.V(0) ... The new helper also swallows ZREM, EXISTS and ZAddNX errors with no logging.' The V(0) log is preexisting hygiene per register; silent helper errors are an observability remark. (ZREM is a write routed to the master, so a persistent READONLY failure is speculative.) Below threshold.

Quote: 'The caller receives N-k entries ... This is pre-existing for skipped orphans, but the PR now makes the number of round trips per page grow with the orphan count on the first listing'. Short pages are preexisting (members counted by ZRangeByLex Count: limit, l.188-193) and the cleanup reduces them on later listings; extra round trips per orphan are ruled non-material in the register ('one-time ZREM+EXISTS per orphan is the PR's intended repair').

Quote: 'The recreated-entry test only covers the empty keyPrefix and only the value-present branch.' True (test l.96-111 uses newTestStore(t, "")); test-coverage observation about a hypothetical future regression, not a product defect.
Quote: 'All new tests are gated behind RUN_REDIS_TESTS=1 and no CI workflow sets it'. Register non_defects: true but test-coverage/hygiene.

Quote: 'Redis expires keys lazily, or on an active-expire cycle with a small delay. On a busy or shared instance ... the test fails with 'redis did not expire the value key'.' Refuted: insertTestEntry (universal_redis_store_test.go:47-57) issues SET ... EX 1 and the test then sleeps 1500ms before EXISTS (l.127-131); the sleep can only run longer under load, and Redis EXISTS performs lazy expiry on access, so a key past its TTL reports 0 whether or not the active-expire cycle has run. No listing precedes the EXISTS, so the logical-expiry branch cannot 'win' first. The asserted spurious failure has no mechanism.

Quote: 'removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember takes both a path and a fileName, which are redundant ... A caller that passes a mismatched path and fileName would ...' API-shape/style remark; the sole caller (l.202-208) passes consistent values. Hypothetical misuse only.

Quote: 'DeleteEntry ... then removes the value and finishes its own ZREM before the listing's ZAddNX runs ... leaving a fresh orphan ... This is benign and self-healing'. Accurate interleaving (l.245-250) whose outcome, as stated, is a transient orphan repaired by the next listing; not a lost live entry. Below threshold.

Quote: 'If the ZAddNX restore fails (connection blip, or a cluster MOVED/READONLY error), the live value has no index member ... Nothing is logged'. The discarded ZAddNX result is true (l.250), but harm requires a concurrent recreate plus a failed restore; go-redis follows MOVED itself. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed' is ruled a non-material narrow hypothetical (needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a failure between back-to-back commands; for a genuine orphan an abandoned restore is correct).
Quote: 'The logical-expiry branch is left unfixed with the same race, and it is the worse variant.' Register non_defects: true but preexisting, disclosed in the PR body, fixed separately.
Quote: 'The new helper takes both path and fileName, although path is derivable ... two different cleanup implementations in one loop.' Maintainability/style remark.

Quote: 'Each orphan costs up to 3 extra sequential round trips ... The glog.V(0) line also still fires once per orphan.' Register non_defects: extra round trips per orphan are the intended one-time repair; the V(0) log is preexisting hygiene.

Quote: 'The tests cannot fail in CI. They all skip without RUN_REDIS_TESTS=1, and the concurrent-recreate test does not exercise the real race or the Exists-error restore branch.' True test-coverage observation; register rules the gating hygiene.

Quote: 'The Redis-expiry test sleeps 1.5s and asserts Redis has already expired the key, which is timing-dependent and can flake under a loaded server ... asserts on the state of the entry before Redis's active or lazy expiry'. Refuted: insertTestEntry (universal_redis_store_test.go:47-57) issues SET ... EX 1 and the test then sleeps 1500ms before EXISTS (l.127-131); the sleep can only run longer under load, and Redis EXISTS performs lazy expiry on access, so a key past its TTL reports 0 whether or not the active-expire cycle has run. No listing precedes the EXISTS, so the logical-expiry branch cannot 'win' first. The asserted spurious failure has no mechanism. The cleanup-leak remark is also empty: the orphan test already DELs the orphan value key (test l.90-92) and the TTL key has expired, so no per-entry value keys remain to leak.

Quote: 'ListDirectoryEntries counts orphan members against limit ... This is pre-existing. The new cleanup makes the effect more visible'. Short pages from skipped orphans exist at the merge-base; the change removes orphans so subsequent pages are fuller, not worse. Preexisting, not introduced by the diff.

Quote: 'with useReadOnly or routeByLatency on redis_cluster2, reads can come from lagging replicas ... The re-check EXISTS is also a read-only command, so it goes to a lagging replica and returns 0, and the helper returns without restoring the member. The live value stays in Redis with no index member. UpdateEntry never re-adds it, so it is invisible to listings and to DeleteFolderChildren ... Before this change that entry was just skipped for one listing.' Exactly GT-s1's mechanism and consequence. Fix is '—' and no corrective change (master-routed check or disabling the cleanup) is proposed anywhere in the item, so absent.

Quote: 'A concurrent insert lands between FindEntry and ZREM. Until the helper's ZAddNX runs, the live entry is missing from the index ... it shows the compensation only converges eventually.' A microsecond transient window that needs a concurrent same-path recreate; register rules the single-view concurrent race converges at the head. The suggested reorder is not tied to replica routing. Below threshold.

Quote: 'The restoring ZAddNX then fails, for example on a network blip, context cancellation or failover. The error is silently dropped.' True (l.250), and correct that the 'retried on next listing' claim covers only the ZREM-failure path, but Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed' is ruled a non-material narrow hypothetical (needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a failure between back-to-back commands; for a genuine orphan an abandoned restore is correct).

Quote: 'The expiry branch still discards Del and ZRem errors, and it has the same concurrent-recreate race with a worse outcome.' Register non_defects: true but preexisting, disclosed, fixed separately (#10744).
Quote: 'The V(0) log still fires for every not-found member ... and the cleanup itself is not logged.' Preexisting log hygiene (l.206) plus an observability suggestion.

Quote: 'The race handling is only tested with a static value present state, and the EXISTS-error and ZAddNX-failure paths are not exercised.' Accurate test-coverage observation (test l.96-111), not a product defect.

Quote: 'sleeps 1.5s for a 1s Redis TTL. On a loaded Redis, or on an entry where the logical expiry wins the race, the value key may still exist. That fails the assertion ... so the test is timing-flaky.' The CI-gating part is true but register-listed hygiene; the flakiness claim, which is the item's asserted consequence, is refuted. Refuted: insertTestEntry (universal_redis_store_test.go:47-57) issues SET ... EX 1 and the test then sleeps 1500ms before EXISTS (l.127-131); the sleep can only run longer under load, and Redis EXISTS performs lazy expiry on access, so a key past its TTL reports 0 whether or not the active-expire cycle has run. No listing precedes the EXISTS, so the logical-expiry branch cannot 'win' first. The asserted spurious failure has no mechanism.

Quote: 'A redis_cluster2 store with useReadOnly or routeByLatency ... The GET and the EXISTS re-check are both replica reads, so both report the value absent, the ZREM on the master succeeds, and the live entry permanently loses its index member ... Before this change lag only skipped one listing.' GT-s1 mechanism and consequence. Fix: 'confirm absence with a read that reaches the master of the value key's slot (for example an EVAL-based EXISTS ...), or skip the cleanup when the cluster client was built with ReadOnly or RouteByLatency' matches the register's accepted shapes. Sufficient.

Quote: 'the ZREM is executed by Redis but its reply is lost or the context ends before the reply is read ... The helper returns on the ZREM error without the EXISTS re-check or ZAddNX restore'. True reading of l.238-240, but harm needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the window plus a lost reply/cancellation. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed' is ruled a non-material narrow hypothetical (needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a failure between back-to-back commands; for a genuine orphan an abandoned restore is correct).

Quote: 'The scaffold documents the replica-read switch as readOnly, but RedisCluster2Store reads useReadOnly'. Accurate (filer.toml:288, redis_cluster_store.go:27,40); register rules it a preexisting config-doc bug outside the diff.
Quote: 'The three new tests skip unless RUN_REDIS_TESTS=1'. True (test l.18-20); register rules it test-coverage hygiene.

Quote: 'redis_cluster2 runs with useReadOnly (or routeByLatency), so the FindEntry GET and the re-check EXISTS go to a replica of the value key's slot while ZREM goes to the index key's master ... The cleanup removes the index member of a live entry and skips the restore. UpdateEntry never re-adds it ... before this change, lag only hid the entry from one listing.' This is GT-s1's mechanism and consequence. Fix: 'run the re-check against the master, for example a single-key EVAL of return redis.call('EXISTS', KEYS[1]) ... or skip the cleanup when the client reads from replicas' is one of the register's accepted shapes. Sufficient.

Quote: 'A concurrent InsertEntry recreates the value, ZREM succeeds, and the restoring ZAddNX fails, for instance on a timeout, a connection error, or a request context cancelled after the ZREM; its error is discarded.' Factually true (l.250) but requires a concurrent recreate plus a failure between back-to-back commands. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed' is ruled a non-material narrow hypothetical (needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a failure between back-to-back commands; for a genuine orphan an abandoned restore is correct).

Quote: 'With redis_cluster2 configured with routeByLatency (or useReadOnly), go-redis sends GET and EXISTS to a replica ... the re-check EXISTS on the same lagging replica returns 0, and the primary ZREM permanently drops the member of a live entry ... where before it was skipped for one listing only.' Same mechanism and consequence as GT-s1 (replica-routed GET l.99 and EXISTS l.245, master ZREM l.238, restore skipped). Fix: 'run the re-check on the primary ... single-key EVAL of EXISTS ... restore the member unless that read confirms the value is absent; alternatively skip the cleanup when the client is configured for replica reads' matches the register's accepted shapes (master-routed single-key Lua EXISTS or disabling cleanup under replica reads). Sufficient.

Quote: 'The restore ZAddNX result is discarded, so a canceled context or connection error after a successful ZREM removes the member without repair, which is narrower than the description's statement'. True (l.250 discards the result) and the item itself frames it as narrow. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed' is ruled a non-material narrow hypothetical (needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a failure between back-to-back commands; for a genuine orphan an abandoned restore is correct).

Quote: 'scaffold/filer.toml documents the replica-read switch as readOnly while redis_cluster2 reads useReadOnly ... this predates the change.' Accurate (redis_cluster_store.go:27,40 vs filer.toml:288); register non_defects rules it a true but preexisting config-doc bug outside the diff.
